transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Recording: Internal Zoom - product-roadmap
Attendees: Priya Nair, Jordan Lee, Alex Kim, Mariana Ruiz, Terry Wu, Sam Patel, Evelyn Cho, Diego Alvarez, Sasha Ivanov, Rina Bose

Summary:
- Final readiness check for upcoming public feature launch (dedicated pools v1, routing policies, and rollout plan).
- Discussed outstanding infra risks (KV cache warmup, autoscale thresholds), compliance items (audit logs, KMS), and QA gaps.
- Agreed on next steps: load testing, canary plan sign-off, and distribute final timeline.

Topics:
1) Launch timeline and gating criteria
2) Infra & capacity (staging tests, autoscale, cache warmup)
3) Security/compliance signoffs (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 items)
4) QA/regression & monitoring (alerts, dashboards)

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya: Okay everybody let's get started, thanks for carving out time. Quick round, if you could say who you are and one thing you need to hear from this call?
[00:08] Jordan: Jordan Lee, eng manager, main thing is we need clarity on canary sizing and traffic split so we can finalize autoscale.
[00:15] Alex: Alex Kim, SRE, I'll be running the load tests so I need the exact config for the dedicated pools and any latency SLOs.
[00:22] Evelyn: Evelyn Cho, eng lead on serving, same - also want to confirm KV cache prewarm expectations, last time we saw cold start spikes.
[00:30] Priya: Great, ok. Quick agenda: timeline, infra risks, compliance, QA, then clear owners. We have 4 weeks til public.

[00:43] Mariana: I put the draft launch timeline in the drive, link in the chat, but it's still draft. See: https://internal.redwood/launch/timeline (note: internal link).
[00:52] Terry: On the timeline, do we have the cutover window for customer migrations? There's some customer-specific routing rules that might complicate things.
[01:00] Sam: We should assume a rolling cutover, not a big bang. Also prioritize customers on Dedicated first, then hosted.

[01:15] Jordan: On canary - proposal is 2.5% traffic for 24 hours, then 10% for 48 hours if no regressions, then 50% for one maintenance window before full. Thoughts?
[01:30] Evelyn: That seems reasonable but we need metric guardrails; latency p95 must stay within 1.2x baseline and error rate under 0.1%. Also, we need fallback routes to smaller quantized models if latency spikes.
[01:45] Alex: I'll set up the dashboards. One question - are we using warm-up requests to prime the KV cache before canary, or relying on natural traffic? Warm-up is preferred.
[01:58] Jordan: Warm-up, yes. We have a script but it's currently tuned for the hosted infra; needs adjustments for Dedicated.

[02:12] Diego: Flag: our E2E regression currently misses some edge cases around streamed responses and function calling. We saw flakiness in the last run.
[02:22] Priya: Ok Diego, can you prioritize those tests and list blockers by EOD Friday?
[02:28] Diego: Yep will do.

[02:35] Rina: On compliance - we need to confirm KMS integration for the private deployment path and the audit log retention. Audit team wants proofs for encryption at rest and who accessed keys.
[02:47] Sasha: We have a KMS plan but HSM integration needs one more review; there's a ticket open.
[02:55] Priya: Rina, can you summarize exact artifacts the auditors want so engineering can prioritize?
[03:01] Rina: I'll send the list, but high level: KMS key rotation policy, access logs, and a proof of network isolation for private deploys.

[03:12] Jordan: Turning to infra risks - last time KV cache entries were evicted under load. We need to bump KV cache size or change eviction TTL for dedicated pools. The tradeoff is memory footprint.
[03:26] Alex: Also observed transient OOM on 80-token context during synthetic workload because of batching behavior. Might be a kernel selection path that regresses with mixed sequence lengths.
[03:38] Terry: Could that be due to the quantization profile? We applied 4-bit quantization in some nodes.
[03:44] Evelyn: Possibly - quantization can change memory patterns. We should run a controlled test matrix: sequence length x quantization x batch size.

[03:56] [04:00] -- Transcript jump --
[04:00] Jordan: For the test matrix, let's capture results in the benchmark sheet, sheet name "staging-matrix-2025-03" - Alex can you drive?
[04:10] Alex: Yeah I'll run it and populate the doc. Will include kernel traces.
[04:18] Priya: On monitoring - what are the key dashboards? Cost per token by route, p95 latency, error rate, KV cache hit rate, and model fallbacks triggered. Any suggestions?
[04:30] Mariana: Add cost by quantization profile too, we've seen 20-30% improvements but need to ensure quality not degraded.
[04:38] Sam: Also include per-customer SLOs for Dedicated tenants.

[04:50] Diego: QA note - the UI for rollout routing still has an edge case when fallback occurs during a partial rollout, some metrics don't tag correctly.
[05:00] Terry: That's probably a tagging bug in the trace pipeline, last commit changed route tagging.
[05:06] Evelyn: We should add an integration test that simulates fallback and asserts metrics tagging.

[05:18] Priya: Ok let's talk about incident readiness and playbooks. Recent incident took 45 minutes to detect, 22 to mitigate. We need better alerting and runbooks.
[05:30] Alex: I propose two alerts: KV cache cold-start spike (p95 increase + cache hit drop) and autoscale lag (queue depth growth). Runbooks should include immediate steps to revert traffic to hosted variant.
[05:44] Jordan: Revert path must be automated with a single button and a rollback TTL. Engineering to build that automation; it'll be part of the canary gating.
[05:55] Priya: Good. Who owns the rollback button?
[05:58] Jordan: Eng infra owns. Alex will build the automation; Terry will review the UI.

[06:08] [06:15] -- 20 minute check-in summary: action items reiterated --
[06:15] Rina: One compliance question - do we need to separate audit logs for Dedicated customers to meet customer-specific retention? Some want 10 years. That's a lot of storage.
[06:28] Priya: We can offer configurable retention as an add-on. Rina to scope storage and cost implications.

[06:38] Mariana: Marketing will need a freeze on messaging until compliance signoff for private deploy features. So timeline gating affects docs, blog, and enablement content.
[06:49] Sam: Noted. We'll pause external comms until we have the signoff.

[06:58] Jordan: Quick tech deep-dive: kernel selection - the runtime currently heuristically picks kernels per sequence length distribution. Under mixed sequences we saw suboptimal picks causing CPU fallback. Need a small change to prefer low-latency kernels for p95-sensitive routes.
[07:18] Evelyn: We should measure any throughput impact; sometimes p95 improvements raise median latency. We'll add that to the matrix.

[07:30] Alex: Load testing plan: run a 72-hour soak at expected peak QPS * 1.5, with sudden 3x bursts to test autoscale. I'll use synthetic keys that mirror prod distribution.
[07:43] Diego: QA will run parallel regression sweeps during the soak to catch functional regressions under load.

[07:52] Priya: Any blockers on the infra tickets? Jordan?
[07:56] Jordan: Two blockers: 1) HSM vendor schedule for KMS integration; 2) final sign-off on memory budget for Dedicated nodes. Both tracked in JIRA - I'll escalate the HSM one.
[08:08] Priya: Good. Please add JIRA links in the recap.

[08:16] Mariana: Ops ask - we need runbooks for support to know who to page during a rollout. Add escalation matrix.
[08:24] Alex: I'll add it to the runbook and post in the incident channel.

[08:30] [08:35] -- Final 10 minutes, recap and owners --
[08:35] Priya: Recap: Priya to send timeline by 3/6; Jordan finalize rollout and SLOs by 3/11; Alex 72-hour load test by 3/7; Diego regression and blockers by 3/9; Rina confirm KMS artifacts by 3/10. Marketing hold until compliance signoff.
[08:55] Sam: Thanks everyone, let's make sure we don't overpromise. We'll schedule a follow-up after load test results.
[09:03] Priya: Meeting adjourned. I'll share notes and the checklist link.

References and shared artifacts mentioned:
- Draft launch timeline: https://internal.redwood/launch/timeline

- Runbook template: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/launch

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K V cache -> KV cache), some speaker labels generic, filler words preserved.

End of transcript.
